name: Julian apples
tile_uses: Raw, slaw on tacos, yogurt, cheese
why_now: Julian is an hour inland and four thousand feet up, and its apples come down the mountain starting in September. A local apple picked this week and eaten raw is a completely different fruit from one that has been in cold storage since last fall — crisper, sharper, and more fragrant.
how_to_choose: Firm all over, with no give when you press near the stem
Smell the blossom end — a fresh apple smells like an apple
Skin should be taut, not waxy or slippery
Small bruises are fine; soft brown patches are not
Ask what came in this week rather than choosing by variety
buy_this_much: 4–5 for the week, and buy more than that if you actually drive up. They keep.
price_note: Mountain apples cost more than the bin at the grocery store, and for the first few weeks of the season they are worth it. By November, the difference narrows.

flavor_paths.name: Raw and cold
flavor_paths.description: Sliced, salted if you like. This is where most of them should go.

flavor_paths.name: Shredded
flavor_paths.description: Into a slaw with lime and cilantro. On tacos, it is a revelation.

flavor_paths.name: With something salty
flavor_paths.description: Sharp cheddar, or a sandwich. Sweetness against salt.

weekday_uses: Shredded into a quick lime-and-cilantro slaw for tacos
Sliced with cheddar and sourdough for lunch
Eaten whole, cold, in the afternoon
weekend_use: A slaw of shredded apple, cabbage, lime, salt, and a lot of cilantro, on the table next to anything you charred.
storage: Refrigerate them. A cold apple keeps for a month and stays crisp; a counter apple goes mealy in a week. Keep them away from anything that absorbs smells.
one_thing_to_learn: Apples are one of the few things in the produce aisle where nothing is truly out of season — but almost everything is out of harvest. Most of the year you are eating fruit that has been held in controlled cold storage for months, which is impressive and also why supermarket apples taste the same in March as in December. September and October are the weeks when you can taste the difference, and the only way to notice it is to eat one raw.
market_question: What came down from the mountain this week?
